citations.assessment: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba reports three rulings Rav Ashi told him from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. The adjacent Rav Ashi statement concerns a different topic.
The checked Bavli gives Rav Assi, or Rabbah ben Issi, speaking in Rav’s name. Heilprin places the notice under early Ashi.
Rabbi Chanina tells Rav Ashi that those north of the Land of Israel should face south. The passage itself poses and answers the question about Babylonia’s location.
The checked chain is Rabbi Zeira from Rabbi Chanina from Rav Ashi from Rabbi. Rabbi Chanina is the likely referent of the initials at this occurrence.
Rav Ashi reports a ruling in Rabbi Shabbatai’s name, to which Rabbi Yochanan objects. Heilprin takes that as evidence for early Ashi.
Reciprocal entry quotes the report and gives its chronological inference.
Rav Huna asks Rav Ashi about the number of sandal nails.
Rav Ashi relates what he observed while before Rav Huna.
Rav Ashi relates an announcement from when he was in Rav Huna’s household.
Rav Huna objects to Rav Ashi’s rule about the wine.
The other entry gives the patronym and calls Chiyya a pupil of Rav. It does not identify every Ashi in the notices here.
The opening ruling reads Ashi. Its resumption in the same digital witness reads Assi.
